messages:
tara: Heads-up — we need to lock the rerank API behavior for top_k and truncation before next sprint planning. Customers keep asking for predictable semantics when they send variable candidate lists.

alex: Yep. Two immediate asks from enterprise customers: 1) stable index-based slicing (return top K of provided candidates) and 2) a normalized-score mode so downstream clients can pick thresholds independent of candidate count.

sasha: Quick reality check — normalization depends on model and candidate count distribution. If we normalize across different candidate set sizes we can distort relative preferences. Need definition: normalize per-request across candidates vs. global calibration.

mike: Ops concern: supporting both modes will change our batching and cache assumptions. If clients expect strict top_k we can short-circuit after scoring K candidates (saves GPU). Normalization forces scoring all candidates then post-process, meaning more work.

tara: Proposal (high level): expose 3 behaviors via ?top_k_mode= in API: "strict" (early exit, return highest-K by streaming score), "normalize" (score all, min-max or softmax normalize across that request), "threshold" (return all above score threshold). Default should be "strict" for perf/backwards compat. Thoughts?

alex: +1 for default strict. Also suggest exposing a header or param to request "full-scores" so clients can opt into normalized scores and we don't have to change default perf.

sasha: For "normalize" we should define the function precisely in spec. Options: per-request softmax on raw logits, per-model z-score using running mean/std, or min-max. Each has tradeoffs: softmax preserves ordering but is sensitive to candidate count; z-score enables cross-request comparability but requires calibration pipeline & storage.

tara: We should include recommended use-cases in spec: - strict = typical ranking UX where you want top-K from provided candidates - normalize = when clients set global score thresholds or combine scores from multiple requests - threshold = low-latency filtering when candidates >> K.

mike: Truncation: need to define both input and candidate token truncation behavior. Are we trimming queries or candidate texts? Current runtime truncates candidate embeddings at 2048 tokens which confuses customers. Recommend we: 1) require clients to send token_count metadata on candidates if they pass long content, 2) have server-side documented truncation policy and return truncated_length in response metadata.

alex: Example request sketch to include in spec:
```json
POST /v1/rerank?top_k=10&top_k_mode=normalize&return_full_scores=true
{
  "query": "How to reset password",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"...", "token_count": 1200},
    {"id":"c2","text":"...", "token_count": 60}
  ]
}
```

sasha: Nice. In responses we should add fields: returned_ids, original_rank, model_score, normalized_score (when requested), truncated_tokens_per_candidate. That gives clients transparency to decide.

tara: Launch criteria draft: - default behavior unchanged (strict) and existing clients unaffected - normalized mode validated against internal bench for calibration drift < 3% on recall @K for our eval set - truncation policy exposed and no silent truncation (response includes truncated_tokens_per_candidate) - perf SLO: normalized mode median latency within 1.8x of strict on typical candidate sizes (<=50).

mike: Can we do a canary where normalized = off by default but enabled for select customers and internal e2e tests? CI-bot: add canary toggle + telemetry for "mode" tag (strict/normalize/threshold).

ci-bot: noted — created canary flag feature/rerank-topk-modes, telemetry event rerank.mode with values [strict, normalize, threshold].

alex: Implementation questions: batching change for normalize probably requires full-scoring micro-batch. We should add a runtime hint param like "max_candidates_for_early_exit" so we can still optimize batches with small candidate counts.

sasha: Calibration story: start with min-max and softmax as experimental; z-score can be Phase 2 once we have per-model running stats. Document expected numerical ranges for each normalization so clients understand meaning.

tara: Action items: - alex: prototype normalized mode with min-max + softmax options (P0) - sasha: design calibration doc & eval metric (recall stability across candidate counts) (P0) - mike: design telemetry and canary rollout plan (P1) - tara: draft API spec text and migration notes + marketing blurb for enterprise customers (P0)

alex: ETA for prototype? 2 weeks for a minimal proof with unit tests and perf bench.

sasha: I'll prepare small eval harness to simulate candidate-set-size skew and measure recall/precision shifts.

tara: Great. We'll review in next product sync. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: One more — add guidance in docs: if clients want cross-request comparability, use normalize+return_full_scores and persist normalized_score for downstream logic.

alex: +1. Also callout cost implications in the spec (normalized mode may be 30-120% higher cost depending on candidate count).

ci-bot: closing note — thread pinned to #product for visibility.
